paper_types.name: Attack
paper_types.definition: A new attack, exploit, leak or inference technique is the main deliverable.

paper_types.name: Defense
paper_types.definition: A new detection, prevention, mitigation, obfuscation or privacy-protection mechanism is the main deliverable.

paper_types.name: Measurement
paper_types.definition: A large-scale empirical characterisation of a threat, an ecosystem or a deployed defense landscape.

paper_types.name: System
paper_types.definition: An implemented system or platform whose engineering properties (overhead, deployment, usability) carry the contribution.

paper_types.name: Analysis or construction
paper_types.definition: A formal result, cryptographic construction, proof, bound or rigorous analysis carries the contribution.

paper_types.name: SoK
paper_types.definition: A systematisation of knowledge: an existing body of work is organised, re-evaluated or unified, and the framework or re-evaluation is the deliverable.

paper_types.name: Dataset or benchmark
paper_types.definition: A dataset, benchmark, testbed or evaluation resource is the main deliverable.

type_order_rule: first yes wins: A6 if the paper systematises or re-evaluates existing work; else A7 if a resource is released as the main artefact; else A1 if the deliverable is an attacker capability; else A3 if the deliverable is a characterisation; else A4 if an implemented artefact carries the claim; else A5 if a formal result carries it; else A2

motivations.definition: A newly deployed technology or protocol creates a threat surface that has not been examined yet (LLMs, QUIC, eBPF, agents, smart contracts).
An existing defense or analysis breaks under a specific, reproducible condition (adaptive attacker, noise, distribution shift, evasion).
Prior work rests on an assumption that no longer holds, for example about attacker capability, threat model, or deployment.
Existing defenses work but cost too much: latency, bandwidth, usability, deployment effort.
No existing method can answer the question at all (a new task, a new granularity, a new platform).
The method works at lab scale or on synthetic data but not on real deployments or real populations.
One structural observation about the problem makes a complex pipeline unnecessary.

intro_codes.L: landscape/context: the deployed reality and who is exposed
intro_codes.C: credit: what prior work does, named, and what it assumes
intro_codes.G: gap: what fails, under which condition, and why
intro_codes.A: attacker model: goal, knowledge, capability, and what is out of scope
intro_codes.I: insight: the observation the design follows from
intro_codes.M: method: the design, components in causal order
intro_codes.S: security or evaluation property: what is guaranteed or measured
intro_codes.R: results: headline numbers with dataset, metric and baseline
intro_codes.P: positioning: the closest work named with one checkable difference
intro_codes.E: ethics and disclosure: IRB, responsible disclosure, data handling, dual use
intro_codes.O: open science: artefact availability, code and data release

reviewer_checks: threat model states goal, knowledge, capability, observables and out-of-scope attacks
an adaptive or knowledgeable attacker is evaluated, not only a static baseline
both error directions reported (attack success and false positives) at a stated operating point
baselines are re-run on the same data with the same budget, and reimplementations are disclosed
overhead (latency, memory, bandwidth) or usability cost is reported next to effectiveness
measurement and human-subject work states IRB approval, data minimisation and responsible disclosure
artefact availability (code, data, evaluation scripts) is stated, with what is withheld and why
claims of robustness name the attack family and the condition they survive
for LLM work, model versions, prompts and decoding settings are disclosed
